BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.

Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Re:** Departures from the Buyer playbook and recommended pushback
**Status:** Internal and privileged. Not for circulation to the Seller.

---

## 1. Preliminary points on how to read the Seller's package

**The "FINAL / settled at principal level" assertion has no effect.** The Seller's preamble says these positions "were settled at principal level by both deal teams" and "are not intended to be re-opened." We should not treat this as true or binding.

- The playbook allows the 20% cap and 18-month fallbacks **only** with prior written authority from Amelia Frost that identifies this draft. None has been given.
- A statement in the counterparty's own covering note is not authority. If anyone on our side believes Amelia has agreed something, confirm it with her directly and in writing before relying on it.
- Until then, every position below is open.

**The "market context" is advocacy, not evidence.** It claims 10–20% caps, ~1% baskets, 12–18 month periods and buyer-knowledge qualifiers are standard. This is unsourced, and it conveniently matches the Seller's positions. Our positions come from the playbook and our DD record, not from the Seller's view of the market. We do not need to engage with it beyond declining to adopt it.

**The Disclosure Letter is stale.** It speaks as at 22 September 2026, about six weeks ago. Several matters (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006) were described as open or preliminary at that date. We should require an updated letter and a bring-down at signing and Completion.

**The Disclosure Letter is more candid than the Seller Update.** On several items the Seller's own disclosure contradicts or undercuts the positions in its covering update:
- Bluefen consent is not in hand.
- Riverlark is not repaid or discharged.
- The bonuses are omitted from the funds flow.
- DD-006 is unresolved.

We should use the Seller's own words against its positions.

---

## 2. Issue-by-issue analysis

### A. Liability regime

| # | Clause | Seller position | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 12.1 Cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | **25% / AUD 6.0m** starting position; 20% only with Amelia Frost written authority (none) | **Reject.** Counter at 25%. |
| 2 | 12.2 De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | **Reject.** 5x our position. |
| 3 | 12.2 Basket | AUD 250,000, excess only ("deductible") | AUD 50,000, **first dollar** once exceeded ("tipping") | **Reject both the level (5x) and the mechanism.** A deductible permanently strips AUD 250k from every recovery. |
| 4 | 12.3 Claims period | 18 months | **24 months**; 18 is a fallback needing Amelia Frost approval (none) | **Reject.** Counter at 24 months. |

**Combined effect.** These provisions together reduce our protection far more than any single one suggests. A AUD 24k claim is irrecoverable. The first AUD 250k of aggregate loss is never recoverable. The ceiling is AUD 1.2m lower. The window is six months shorter. We should present all four as a package and not trade them off individually.

### B. Hidden general-regime overrides

**5. Clause 12.3/13: "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."**
This is the most dangerous drafting point in the package. Its practical effect is that the general cap, basket, de minimis and time limit would sweep in:
- title and capacity claims
- tax and IP claims
- specific indemnities (including Ironquay)
- covenant breaches
- payment obligations (e.g. leakage or price adjustment), and potentially fraud.

Any category we forget to carve out expressly would fall into the general regime by default. That inverts the playbook, which requires the categories to be kept separate with no hidden override.

**Recommendation:** Delete it. Instead, the general limitations should apply **only** to "General Warranty Claims" as a defined term. Each other category should carry its own regime.

**6. Fundamental / Title warranties on the same caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity."**
Reject. The playbook requires a separate regime for title and capacity:
- 100% cap (AUD 24m)
- at least six years
- outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.

Title is the thing we are paying for. A 20% cap on a title failure would mean paying AUD 24m and recovering at most AUD 4.8m. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept that.

**7. Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5: limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature."**
Reject. As drafted, this would purport to cap and time-bar claims for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct. It would also use non-reliance to shut out misrepresentation claims grounded in fraud.

Under the playbook, these matters must be carved out of all of the following, to the maximum extent enforceable:
- caps
- baskets
- time limits
- exclusive remedies
- non-reliance.

This is not negotiable, and no one on our team has authority to waive it.

Note that some protection may exist regardless (for example, statutory misleading or deceptive conduct protections and the general law on fraud). We should not rely on that. The carve-out must be express.

*Suggested language:* "Nothing in this agreement (including clauses 9.3, 12, 13 and 20.5) limits or excludes any liability of the Seller, or any Claim by the Buyer, arising from fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct of the Seller, its officers, employees, agents or advisers."

**8. Tax / IP: "settled under the general regime."**
Reject the characterisation. Tax and IP terms remain **open** on our side. They have not been resolved, and they are not to be folded into the general regime by default.

Equally, we should not overclaim. Our records do not assume an agreed position of unlimited liability for these categories. Respond simply that the tax and IP regimes remain open for negotiation as separate categories.

### C. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

**9. Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2]: general disclosure of the entire data room, the Accounts, the statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."**
Reject. The playbook requires **specific, fair disclosure**. Whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure means any document anywhere in DD-002 to DD-012, or on any public register, qualifies every warranty. The warranties would become largely illusory, and the burden of finding problems would shift entirely to us.

**Recommendation:**
- Delete [1.1] and [1.2].
- Disclosure should qualify warranties only where it is made against a specific warranty, with sufficient detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely effect.
- The specific disclosures (paras 2–10) can stand as specific disclosures, subject to the points below.

**Para [1.4], the non-admission language,** is broadly acceptable as a non-admission clause. It must not, however, be read as qualifying the warranties or as a disclaimer that consents or discharges are unnecessary.

**10. Clause 8.3: Buyer knowledge, including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records."**
Reject. This is a blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion, stretched further by a constructive "discoverable" standard. It would let the Seller defeat claims on the matters it has itself flagged as open, such as Bluefen, Riverlark and DD-006.

**Recommendation:** Delete clause 8.3. If a knowledge qualifier is conceded anywhere, it must:
- be **Seller** knowledge, limited to **named individuals**, after **reasonable enquiry**; and
- **never** apply to title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

### D. Conditions precedent and completion mechanics

**11. Bluefen consent (clauses 3 / 6.3): reasonable endeavours; satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent."**
Reject. According to the Seller's own disclosure (para 2):
- Bluefen accounts for about **AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue, roughly 30%** of the business;
- consent is required under clause 11.2, subject to **conditions in 11.3**; and
- no final consent and **no evidence those conditions are satisfied** has been provided.

Under consent-on-delivery, we could be obliged to complete on a consent whose conditions are unmet, which may leave the consent ineffective or the contract terminable. Reasonable endeavours alone is inadequate for a customer of this size.

**Recommendation:**
- Make it a condition precedent that an **effective** Bluefen consent has been obtained **and** that evidence satisfactory to the Buyer shows the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied, both before Completion.
- Strengthen the Seller's obligation beyond reasonable endeavours, for example to "all reasonable endeavours" plus a positive obligation to satisfy the 11.3 conditions within its control.
- The condition should be waivable by the Buyer only.

**12. Riverlark facility (clauses 2 / 7): a release "to be provided following Completion."**
Reject. The Seller's disclosure (para 3) confirms:
- about **AUD 3.2m outstanding**;
- change-control (clause 8.1) and discharge (clause 9.2) provisions apply; and
- the facility is **not repaid** and **no discharge** is in hand.

On a debt-free basis, a post-Completion release would leave us owning a company whose assets remain encumbered and whose lender may have change-of-control rights. Our only protection would be a promise.

**Recommendation:**
- Require a current **payout letter**.
- Require **direct repayment to Riverlark from Completion funds**, deducted from the price in the funds flow.
- Require **executed security releases and discharges** (including PPSR releases) delivered at Completion.
- A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an **irrevocable undertaking** from the lender **and** written approval from Amelia Frost. Neither has been offered.

**13. Funds flow: DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised.**
Reject. This is exactly the silent exclusion the playbook prohibits. The bonuses are Completion-triggered liabilities of the **Company** (disclosure para 5), and they will crystallise in the business we own. If they are not itemised, they will land on us after Completion, together with any payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs. The Seller's disclosure expressly declines to address those on-costs.

**Recommendation:**
- The AUD 420,000 and **all triggered on-costs** must either be a specific line item in the funds flow (deducted from price, paid through payroll at Completion) or be expressly Seller-funded, backed by an indemnity.
- Require the Seller to confirm the on-cost position.

### E. Specific risk items

**14. Ironquay IP (clause 11.1): indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment, "considered adequate."**
Reject as too narrow. The disclosure (para 4) confirms:
- transfer of SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee;
- DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; and
- no receipt and no confirmatory assignment exist.

If transfer has not occurred, the risk is not just the unpaid fee. It extends to ownership of, and the right to use, the Project Materials, and to third-party claims or remediation costs.

**Recommendation:**
- Broaden the indemnity to cover losses arising from any failure of the Company to own, or hold sufficient rights to, the Ironquay deliverables.
- Preserve the **SOW3 cure**: payment of the outstanding fees plus delivery of a confirmatory assignment, ideally as a Completion deliverable.
- Keep the indemnity outside the general cap and basket.

*Caution:* the AUD 180,000 has **not been independently verified**, in either direction. DD-010 is not bank evidence, as the Seller concedes. We should not assert that the amount is definitely unpaid or definitely accurate. Instead, require evidence: bank records, Ironquay's statement of account, or confirmation from Ironquay.

**15. DD-006 export/privacy incident (clause 4.6 / Schedule 6): "not expected to be material."**
Do not accept the characterisation. Equally, we should not overstate the position ourselves.

On the record (para 6), a download link was sent to an unintended external address. The export may contain about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September it was **unknown** whether there was access, what the exact scope was, or whether notification is required. There is no confirmed breach, no confirmed harm, no established notification duty and no loss amount. Our requests should be framed neutrally.

**Recommendation:**
- Require preservation of all logs and evidence.
- Require completion of the investigation, with regular written updates before Completion and an updated disclosure at bring-down.
- Require the Seller to cooperate with any notifiability assessment.
- Seek appropriate contractual protection, for example a specific indemnity for losses arising from the incident, or at minimum a warranty and covenant regime that the "not material" framing does not water down.

Do **not** put a number on it or assert that a breach has occurred.

**16. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): "ordinary-course operating costs."**
Assess; do not accept or reject reflexively. The disclosure (para 8) says the three related renewals (AUD 110,000 each, DD-008 / DD-011) should be read together, and it does not state whether each one is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

The Seller's label is an assertion, but our playbook equally does **not** treat these renewals automatically as Debt or as a price deduction.

**Recommendation:** Request the underlying contracts and information on timing, termination rights, accrual treatment and the commercial rationale for the three related renewals. Then decide on treatment in the completion accounts, leakage or warranties. Do not concede "ordinary course" in the meantime.

**17. Title: share register (DD-012) as evidence.**
Reject as insufficient. DD-012 is a Seller-supplied internal record. The Seller's own disclosure (para 10) concedes that it merely "identifies the source relied on" and that we have not verified it.

**Recommendation:** Require independent evidence, including:
- an ASIC company extract consistent with the register;
- share certificates (or confirmation of uncertificated status);
- the history of issues and transfers, with supporting resolutions;
- PPSR searches against the Company and the Seller over the shares;
- confirmation that no options, rights or encumbrances exist; and
- evidence of the Seller's corporate authority (board resolution) and capacity.

All of this should sit behind title warranties in the separate fundamental regime described in point 6.

**18. Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).**
These are not playbook items. The Seller's disclosure characterises the lease as a notification obligation only and Mossvale as an assignment restriction not triggered by a share sale. These readings may be right, but they are the Seller's characterisations. Ask our counsel to confirm them against the actual change-of-control and assignment provisions. Include the lease notification as a Completion or post-Completion deliverable as appropriate.

---

## 3. Summary of recommendations

**Overarching**
1. Do not treat any position as "FINAL" or principal-agreed. No written authority from Amelia Frost exists for any fallback. Escalate to her if the Seller insists.
2. Require an updated Disclosure Letter, since the current one dates from 22 Sept 2026, plus a bring-down at signing and Completion.

**Liability (send back as a package)**
3. Cap: **25% / AUD 6.0m** (reject 20%).
4. De minimis **AUD 5,000**; basket **AUD 50,000, tipping to first dollar** (reject AUD 25k and the AUD 250k deductible).
5. General claims period: **24 months** (reject 18).
6. Delete the "limitations apply to all Claims" default in 12.3/13. General limitations should apply only to General Warranty Claims.
7. Title and capacity: **separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years**, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
8. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: **express carve-out** from all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5). Non-negotiable.
9. Tax and IP: remain **open** as separate categories. Reject "settled under the general regime." Do not assert any agreed position.

**Disclosure and knowledge**
10. Delete general disclosure ([1.1]–[1.2]). Accept only specific, fair disclosure.
11. Delete clause 8.3. Any knowledge qualifier must use named Seller persons and reasonable enquiry, and must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or indemnities.

**Completion**
12. Bluefen: CP for an **effective consent plus evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied** before Completion, with a stronger obligation than reasonable endeavours.
13. Riverlark: payout letter, **direct repayment from Completion funds**, and executed releases at Completion. No post-Completion release without an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
14. Bonuses: **AUD 420,000 plus on-costs** as a specific funds-flow line item or expressly Seller-funded and indemnified.

**Specific risks**
15. Ironquay: broaden the indemnity beyond the SOW3 payment, preserve the SOW3 cure (payment plus confirmatory assignment), and verify the AUD 180,000 independently.
16. DD-006: preservation, investigation and update obligations, plus appropriate specific protection. Keep the framing neutral: no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or amount.
17. Sandbar: request information and assess. No automatic Debt or price treatment, and no concession of "ordinary course."
18. Title: independent evidence of title, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 alone is insufficient.
19. Lease and Mossvale: our counsel to verify the Seller's characterisations against the source provisions.

**Items to escalate to Amelia Frost:** any Seller insistence on the 20% cap or 18-month period, and any proposal for a post-Completion Riverlark release. The fraud carve-out is not hers or anyone's to waive, but she should be told if the Seller resists it.

Under the playbook, these matters must be carved out of all of the following, to the maximum extent enforceable:
- caps
- baskets
- time limits
- exclusive remedies
- non-reliance.

This is not negotiable, and no one on our team has authority to waive it.

Note that some protection may exist regardless (for example, statutory misleading or deceptive conduct protections and the general law on fraud). We should not rely on that. The carve-out must be express.

*Suggested language:* "Nothing in this agreement (including clauses 9.3, 12, 13 and 20.5) limits or excludes any liability of the Seller, or any Claim by the Buyer, arising from fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct of the Seller, its officers, employees, agents or advisers."

**8. Tax / IP: "settled under the general regime."**
Reject the characterisation. Tax and IP terms remain **open** on our side. They have not been resolved, and they are not to be folded into the general regime by default.

Equally, we should not overclaim. Our records do not assume an agreed position of unlimited liability for these categories. Respond simply that the tax and IP regimes remain open for negotiation as separate categories.

### C. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

**9. Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2]: general disclosure of the entire data room, the Accounts, the statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."**
Reject. The playbook requires **specific, fair disclosure**. Whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure means any document anywhere in DD-002 to DD-012, or on any public register, qualifies every warranty. The warranties would become largely illusory, and the burden of finding problems would shift entirely to us.

**Recommendation:**
- Delete [1.1] and [1.2].
- Disclosure should qualify warranties only where it is made against a specific warranty, with sufficient detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely effect.
- The specific disclosures (paras 2–10) can stand as specific disclosures, subject to the points below.

**Para [1.4], the non-admission language,** is broadly acceptable as a non-admission clause. It must not, however, be read as qualifying the warranties or as a disclaimer that consents or discharges are unnecessary.

**10. Clause 8.3: Buyer knowledge, including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records."**
Reject. This is a blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion, stretched further by a constructive "discoverable" standard. It would let the Seller defeat claims on the matters it has itself flagged as open, such as Bluefen, Riverlark and DD-006.

**Recommendation:** Delete clause 8.3. If a knowledge qualifier is conceded anywhere, it must:
- be **Seller** knowledge, limited to **named individuals**, after **reasonable enquiry**; and
- **never** apply to title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

### D. Conditions precedent and completion mechanics

**11. Bluefen consent (clauses 3 / 6.3): reasonable endeavours; satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent."**
Reject. According to the Seller's own disclosure (para 2):
- Bluefen accounts for about **AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue, roughly 30%** of the business;
- consent is required under clause 11.2, subject to **conditions in 11.3**; and
- no final consent and **no evidence those conditions are satisfied** has been provided.

Under consent-on-delivery, we could be obliged to complete on a consent whose conditions are unmet, which may leave the consent ineffective or the contract terminable. Reasonable endeavours alone is inadequate for a customer of this size.

**Recommendation:**
- Make it a condition precedent that an **effective** Bluefen consent has been obtained **and** that evidence satisfactory to the Buyer shows the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied, both before Completion.
- Strengthen the Seller's obligation beyond reasonable endeavours, for example to "all reasonable endeavours" plus a positive obligation to satisfy the 11.3 conditions within its control.
- The condition should be waivable by the Buyer only.

**12. Riverlark facility (clauses 2 / 7): a release "to be provided following Completion."**
Reject. The Seller's disclosure (para 3) confirms:
- about **AUD 3.2m outstanding**;
- change-control (clause 8.1) and discharge (clause 9.2) provisions apply; and
- the facility is **not repaid** and **no discharge** is in hand.

On a debt-free basis, a post-Completion release would leave us owning a company whose assets remain encumbered and whose lender may have change-of-control rights. Our only protection would be a promise.

**Recommendation:**
- Require a current **payout letter**.
- Require **direct repayment to Riverlark from Completion funds**, deducted from the price in the funds flow.
- Require **executed security releases and discharges** (including PPSR releases) delivered at Completion.
- A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an **irrevocable undertaking** from the lender **and** written approval from Amelia Frost. Neither has been offered.

**13. Funds flow: DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised.**
Reject. This is exactly the silent exclusion the playbook prohibits. The bonuses are Completion-triggered liabilities of the **Company** (disclosure para 5), and they will crystallise in the business we own. If they are not itemised, they will land on us after Completion, together with any payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs. The Seller's disclosure expressly declines to address those on-costs.

**Recommendation:**
- The AUD 420,000 and **all triggered on-costs** must either be a specific line item in the funds flow (deducted from price, paid through payroll at Completion) or be expressly Seller-funded, backed by an indemnity.
- Require the Seller to confirm the on-cost position.

### E. Specific risk items

**14. Ironquay IP (clause 11.1): indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment, "considered adequate."**
Reject as too narrow. The disclosure (para 4) confirms:
- transfer of SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee;
- DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; and
- no receipt and no confirmatory assignment exist.

If transfer has not occurred, the risk is not just the unpaid fee. It extends to ownership of, and the right to use, the Project Materials, and to third-party claims or remediation costs.

**Recommendation:**
- Broaden the indemnity to cover losses arising from any failure of the Company to own, or hold sufficient rights to, the Ironquay deliverables.
- Preserve the **SOW3 cure**: payment of the outstanding fees plus delivery of a confirmatory assignment, ideally as a Completion deliverable.
- Keep the indemnity outside the general cap and basket.

*Caution:* the AUD 180,000 has **not been independently verified**, in either direction. DD-010 is not bank evidence, as the Seller concedes. We should not assert that the amount is definitely unpaid or definitely accurate. Instead, require evidence: bank records, Ironquay's statement of account, or confirmation from Ironquay.

**15. DD-006 export/privacy incident (clause 4.6 / Schedule 6): "not expected to be material."**
Do not accept the characterisation. Equally, we should not overstate the position ourselves.

On the record (para 6), a download link was sent to an unintended external address. The export may contain about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September it was **unknown** whether there was access, what the exact scope was, or whether notification is required. There is no confirmed breach, no confirmed harm, no established notification duty and no loss amount. Our requests should be framed neutrally.

**Recommendation:**
- Require preservation of all logs and evidence.
- Require completion of the investigation, with regular written updates before Completion and an updated disclosure at bring-down.
- Require the Seller to cooperate with any notifiability assessment.
- Seek appropriate contractual protection, for example a specific indemnity for losses arising from the incident, or at minimum a warranty and covenant regime that the "not material" framing does not water down.

Do **not** put a number on it or assert that a breach has occurred.

**16. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): "ordinary-course operating costs."**
Assess; do not accept or reject reflexively. The disclosure (para 8) says the three related renewals (AUD 110,000 each, DD-008 / DD-011) should be read together, and it does not state whether each one is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

The Seller's label is an assertion, but our playbook equally does **not** treat these renewals automatically as Debt or as a price deduction.

**Recommendation:** Request the underlying contracts and information on timing, termination rights, accrual treatment and the commercial rationale for the three related renewals. Then decide on treatment in the completion accounts, leakage or warranties. Do not concede "ordinary course" in the meantime.

**17. Title: share register (DD-012) as evidence.**
Reject as insufficient. DD-012 is a Seller-supplied internal record. The Seller's own disclosure (para 10) concedes that it merely "identifies the source relied on" and that we have not verified it.

**Recommendation:** Require independent evidence, including:
- an ASIC company extract consistent with the register;
- share certificates (or confirmation of uncertificated status);
- the history of issues and transfers, with supporting resolutions;
- PPSR searches against the Company and the Seller over the shares;
- confirmation that no options, rights or encumbrances exist; and
- evidence of the Seller's corporate authority (board resolution) and capacity.

All of this should sit behind title warranties in the separate fundamental regime described in point 6.

**18. Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).**
These are not playbook items. The Seller's disclosure characterises the lease as a notification obligation only and Mossvale as an assignment restriction not triggered by a share sale. These readings may be right, but they are the Seller's characterisations. Ask our counsel to confirm them against the actual change-of-control and assignment provisions. Include the lease notification as a Completion or post-Completion deliverable as appropriate.

## 3. Summary of recommendations

**Overarching**
1. Do not treat any position as "FINAL" or principal-agreed. No written authority from Amelia Frost exists for any fallback. Escalate to her if the Seller insists.
2. Require an updated Disclosure Letter, since the current one dates from 22 Sept 2026, plus a bring-down at signing and Completion.

**Liability (send back as a package)**
3. Cap: **25% / AUD 6.0m** (reject 20%).
4. De minimis **AUD 5,000**; basket **AUD 50,000, tipping to first dollar** (reject AUD 25k and the AUD 250k deductible).
5. General claims period: **24 months** (reject 18).
6. Delete the "limitations apply to all Claims" default in 12.3/13. General limitations should apply only to General Warranty Claims.
7. Title and capacity: **separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years**, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
8. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: **express carve-out** from all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5). Non-negotiable.
9. Tax and IP: remain **open** as separate categories. Reject "settled under the general regime." Do not assert any agreed position.

**Disclosure and knowledge**
10. Delete general disclosure ([1.1]–[1.2]). Accept only specific, fair disclosure.
11. Delete clause 8.3. Any knowledge qualifier must use named Seller persons and reasonable enquiry, and must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or indemnities.

**Completion**
12. Bluefen: CP for an **effective consent plus evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied** before Completion, with a stronger obligation than reasonable endeavours.
13. Riverlark: payout letter, **direct repayment from Completion funds**, and executed releases at Completion. No post-Completion release without an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
14. Bonuses: **AUD 420,000 plus on-costs** as a specific funds-flow line item or expressly Seller-funded and indemnified.

**Specific risks**
15. Ironquay: broaden the indemnity beyond the SOW3 payment, preserve the SOW3 cure (payment plus confirmatory assignment), and verify the AUD 180,000 independently.
16. DD-006: preservation, investigation and update obligations, plus appropriate specific protection. Keep the framing neutral: no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or amount.
17. Sandbar: request information and assess. No automatic Debt or price treatment, and no concession of "ordinary course."
18. Title: independent evidence of title, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 alone is insufficient.
19. Lease and Mossvale: our counsel to verify the Seller's characterisations against the source provisions.

**Items to escalate to Amelia Frost:** any Seller insistence on the 20% cap or 18-month period, and any proposal for a post-Completion Riverlark release. The fraud carve-out is not hers or anyone's to waive, but she should be told if the Seller resists it.
